name: Sebuda
title: Mother of King Jehoiakim of Judah
summary: Sebuda (also spelled Sebudda) was the daughter of Pedaiah from Rimmon and the mother of Eliakim (Jehoiakim), who was installed as king over Judah by Pharaoh Neco II. She is mentioned in connection with the kings during Judah's final days, a time marked by political unrest and Babylon's growing power.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as mother of Eliakim (Jehoiakim)
keyEvents.description: Sebuda is mentioned as the daughter of Pedaiah from Rimmon and the mother of Eliakim, who later was installed as king under the name Jehoiakim by Pharaoh Neco.

keyEvents.title: Josiah's reign and death
keyEvents.description: Sebuda was one of King Josiah's wives. Josiah fell in battle at Megiddo against Pharaoh Neco II, which changed the fate of the entire royal family.

keyEvents.title: Jehoiakim is installed as king
keyEvents.description: After Pharaoh Neco deposed Jehoahaz, he installed Eliakim son of Shaphan as king over Judah and gave him the name Jehoiakim.

keyEvents.title: Jehoiakim's Reign and Idolatry
keyEvents.description: Jehoiakim son of Shaphan reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, but he did what was evil in the Lord's sight.

keyEvents.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Invasion During Jehoiakim's Reign
keyEvents.description: During Jehoiakim's reign, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came and attacked Judah, marking the beginning of Babylonian dominance over the land.
